summary.whatChanges: In Zod v4's lazy failure result, the captured raw issues and parse context are dropped once the `error` is built by the getter or assigned via the setter, so a retained `safeParse` failure result no longer keeps the parsed input alive. A GC-based test verifies the release.
behaviorChanges: Holding a failed safeParse result no longer retains a strong reference to the parsed input value after the error is read or replaced, reducing memory retention.
Assigning `result.error` also releases the internal issues/context, not just reading it.
New test uses V8 flags and forced GC to assert the parsed inputs become collectable.
risks: If `result.error` is set to a falsy value (e.g. undefined) after the captures are cleared, the getter re-enters the build branch and would throw on `issues.map` of undefined.
Any future code path needing `issues` or `ctx` after first error access will now see undefined.
The GC test relies on v8.setFlagsFromString('--expose-gc') and timing heuristics, which can be flaky or environment-dependent in CI.
Error construction is now effectively one-shot; repeated lazy rebuilds are no longer possible.
